audits.title: 900 A Single-Centre 2-Cycle Audit of Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumour Post-Operative Documentation
audits.standard: Standard checklist by Kikuchi et al

cycle1.result: Pre-op rectal examination recorded in 24%; tumour number 40%; completeness of resection 32%; tumour location 96%.

audits.intervention: Teaching session at departmental teaching and a template operation note.
audits.other_findings: Described as a 2-cycle audit but second-cycle results not given.
audits.citation: Singh P, Price J, Abdel Latif M, Suntharasivam T. 900 A Single-Centre 2-Cycle Audit of Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumour Post-Operative Documentation. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.289.

audits.title: 953 Improving Documentation of Operation Notes for Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumour: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.setting: General hospital in London (Homerton University Hospital)

cycle1.result: Number of tumours 86.21%; size of largest tumour 65.52%; recurrent or primary 31.03%; CIS assessment 3.45%; clinical stage 10.34%; separate base biopsy 10.34%; detrusor muscle visualisation 71.43%.

audits.intervention: 12-point standardised TURBT operation note template introduced June 2024.

cycle2.result: Number of tumours 100%; size 88.89%; recurrent or primary 66.67%; CIS assessment 55.56%; clinical stage 55.56%; base biopsy 66.67%; detrusor muscle visualisation 55.56%.

audits.other_findings: Detrusor muscle visualisation documentation fell (71.43% vs 55.56%).
audits.citation: Shah D, Tien T, Henderson S, Pati J. 953 Improving Documentation of Operation Notes for Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumour: A Closed Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.726.

audits.title: 973 Assessing the Quality of TURBT: A Comprehensive 18-Month Audit from a UK District General Hospital
audits.standard: BAUS and EAU guideline standards, including detrusor muscle present in 70% of specimens (BAUS) and EAU indications for re-resection
audits.setting: East Surrey Hospital, Redhill; district general hospital

cycle1.result: Detrusor muscle present in 55.4% (below BAUS 70% standard); tumour number documented in 86%, size in 84%, completeness of resection in 78%; MMC given in 53.5% of all cases and 58.8% of eligible NMIBC; 39 of 43 re-TURBTs met EAU indications.

audits.intervention: Planned: standardised TURBT operative template and targeted education, with re-audit to follow.
audits.other_findings: Residual tumour at re-TURBT in seven patients and one upstaged from T1 to T2; recurrences in nine patients at 3 months and eight at 12 months, mainly high-risk.
audits.citation: Das S. 973 Assessing the Quality of TURBT: A Comprehensive 18-Month Audit from a UK District General Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.261.

audits.title: How well do we manage non-muscle invasive bladder tumors? A UK audit of real-life practices.
audits.standard: Guidelines on management of non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (single instillation chemotherapy, re-TUR timing)
audits.setting: Urology Department, The Pennine Acute Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Detrusor muscle absent in 22.8% of initial TURBT specimens; single instillation chemotherapy given to only 40% of eligible patients; 54.3% had re-TUR, on average 10 weeks after TURBT; 3-month recurrence 36.0%.

audits.other_findings: Tumours over 3 cm and carcinoma in situ predicted early recurrence.
audits.citation: Sountoulides P, Mutomba WF, Bouras E, Lim J, Bourdoumis A, Jain A. How well do we manage non-muscle invasive bladder tumors? A UK audit of real-life practices. Urologia. 2020;87(3):142-148. doi:10.1177/0391560319899303. PMID: 31959070.

audits.title: Improving the Quality of Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumour (TURBT) Operative Notes Following the European Association of Urology Guidelines: A Completed Audit Loop Study.
audits.standard: European Association of Urology 2022 guidelines for TURBT documentation
audits.setting: District general hospital, UK (Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: Tumour size 46%, tumour description 59%, depth of resection 36%, chemotherapy 21%, perforation assessment 22%, completeness of resection 59%, pre-op EUA 47%, post-op EUA 14%

audits.intervention: Standardised TURBT operation note template with staff training

cycle2.result: Tumour size 89%, description 89%, depth 89%, chemotherapy 46%, perforation 68% (p=0.001), completeness 68% (p=0.42), pre- and post-op EUA 89%

audits.other_findings: Completeness of resection improvement was not statistically significant.
audits.citation: Guerero DN, Bruce A, Vayalapra S, Menon V, El Hadi M, Khashaba S. Improving the Quality of Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumour (TURBT) Operative Notes Following the European Association of Urology Guidelines: A Completed Audit Loop Study. Cureus. 2022;14(10):e30131. doi:10.7759/cureus.30131. PMID: 36246089.

audits.title: Improving the quality of transurethral resection of bladder tumour (TURBT) operative notes following the European Association of Urology guidelines.
audits.standard: European Association of Urology guideline documentation criteria for TURBT
audits.setting: Department of Urology, St. James's Hospital, Dublin (academic teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 69%; tumour appearance 65%, size 67.5%, completeness of resection 55%, complications 2.5%.

audits.intervention: Standardised electronic TURBT operative note template based on EAU guidelines.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 93%; tumour appearance 97.5%, size 90%, completeness of resection 95%, complications 75%.

audits.title: Impact of audit and feedback on transurethral resection of bladder tumour quality: a monocentric post-completion evaluation of the RESECT trial.
audits.standard: Four RESECT surgical quality indicators: detrusor muscle sampling, completeness of resection, accuracy of operative documentation, and single immediate intravesical chemotherapy
audits.setting: Tertiary university hospital (Fondazione Policlinico Tor Vergata), monocentric prospective cohort

cycle1.result: Detrusor muscle presence 61.9% in the pre-audit phase; 70.7% during the prospective audit phase (128 patients across all phases, March 2023 to June 2025)

audits.intervention: Participation in the RESECT audit and feedback programme

cycle2.result: Detrusor muscle presence 85.9% in the post-audit phase

audits.other_findings: Improvements in quality indicators were sustained after programme completion but did not yield a detectable reduction in recurrence.
audits.citation: Orecchia L, Gerardi M, Colalillo G, Leonardis F, Rosato E, Asimakopoulos AD, et al.. Impact of audit and feedback on transurethral resection of bladder tumour quality: a monocentric post-completion evaluation of the RESECT trial. BJU Int. 2026;138(1):92-99. doi:10.1111/bju.70266. PMID: 41919786.
